name: BioGrapher
tagline: Paste your data and make publication-ready plots, with significance brackets you drag into place.
summary: BioGrapher is a plotting app for biologists. Paste data into a spreadsheet grid, mark what the rows and columns mean, and it becomes a plot-ready table in one click.
Split, filter and recolour plots directly. Drag across groups to add significance brackets. Arrange figures over several pages and export them as editable SVG or PNG.

highlights.title: Ready to plot in one click
highlights.body: Mark what the rows and columns mean, and the table is reshaped for plotting.

highlights.title: 20+ chart types
highlights.body: Scatter, bar, box, violin, heatmap, 3D and survival plots, plus curve fitting for dose-response, Michaelis–Menten and binding.

highlights.title: Drag to add significance
highlights.body: Drag across the groups you want to compare to add significance brackets.

highlights.title: Editable exports
highlights.body: SVG exports stay editable in vector drawing programs such as Illustrator or Inkscape.

os.Other: Build from source with Node.js 20+, Python 3.12 and uv

hardware.Disk: Extra space for the built-in Python engine

name: OmicExplorer
tagline: Explore proteomics and other omic data: build an analysis as a workflow of steps, then explore linked, interactive plots.
metaTitle: OmicExplorer — Desktop app for proteomics and omic data
metaDescription: Explore proteomics and other omic data. Build an analysis as a workflow of steps, then explore linked, interactive plots. Free for macOS and Windows.

launchTips.intro: OmicExplorer is not signed by Apple or Microsoft, so your computer may block it at first. To open it:

steps.text: Double-click the app. When it says it can't be opened, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
Right-click the app, choose Open, then click Open again.
Click More info, then Run anyway.
Right-click the .exe, choose Properties, tick Unblock at the bottom, click OK, then run it.

summary: Load your own data, or turn one raw export from DIA-NN, Spectronaut or MaxQuant into ready-to-use files with the guided import. Annotations such as GO, KEGG, Reactome and STRING are fetched for you.

Build the analysis as a workflow of steps: clean data, compare, contrast and curve fit. Save it all in one project file. Results open in a dashboard of linked plots, where hovering or pinning a gene highlights it everywhere. Export plots as SVG, PNG or PDF and tables as CSV or XLSX.

highlights.title: Workflow editor
highlights.body: Chain steps such as Load data, Clean data and Compare on a canvas. Save the whole analysis in one project file.

highlights.title: Guided import
highlights.body: Turn a raw DIA-NN, Spectronaut or MaxQuant export into data, samplesheet and metadata files. Annotations are fetched for you.

highlights.title: Built-in statistics
highlights.body: Filtering, imputation, normalisation and batch correction, then t-tests, ANOVA, contrasts and dose or time curve fits.

highlights.title: Linked plots
highlights.body: Volcano, heatmap, PCA, enrichment, STRING network and more. Hover or pin a gene to highlight it in every plot.

highlights.title: Local and private
highlights.body: Runs on your computer with no Python, server or account. Your data never leaves your machine.

highlights.title: Editable exports
highlights.body: Plots as SVG, PNG or PDF, with shapes that stay editable in Illustrator. Tables as CSV or XLSX.

os.Other: Build from source with git and Node.js

hardware.Memory: Data is held in memory, so large datasets need more RAM
hardware.Data: A data matrix (CSV). A samplesheet and metadata file are optional. Or one raw DIA-NN, Spectronaut or MaxQuant export

name: UniOme
tagline: Browse gene, protein, interaction and pathway data for bacteria, offline on your own computer.
summary: UniOme brings together annotation from about 30 public databases in one app: genes, protein and RNA structures, interactions, regulation and pathways. All data is stored on your computer, so it works offline with no server or account.

Four organisms are included: Escherichia coli K-12, Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv, Staphylococcus aureus NCTC 8325 and Bacillus subtilis 168. More will be added, and the build scripts in the repository can add new ones.

highlights.title: About 30 databases in one place
highlights.body: Annotation from about 30 databases, linked gene by gene.

highlights.title: Works offline
highlights.body: No server, account or internet connection needed. The data comes with the app.

highlights.title: Structure next to function
highlights.body: See protein and RNA structures alongside interactions, regulation and pathways for each gene.

highlights.title: Clear data sources
highlights.body: The source, licence and citation of every dataset are documented.

hardware.Disk: Several GB for the included data

citation.text: yjzhng (2026). UniOme: a local-first annotation-database browser for prokaryotes. Version 0.1.0. https://github.com/yjzhng/UniOme

name: prokDB
tagline: Build one gene annotation table for any prokaryote from NCBI, UniProt and KEGG, in a desktop app or on the command line.
summary: Enter a taxonomy ID and prokDB merges NCBI RefSeq and GenBank genome features, UniProt protein annotation and KEGG pathways into one CSV table. It can also predict where each protein is located in the cell, using DeepLocPro on your computer.
The desktop app and the command line run the same seven-step pipeline. Run steps one at a time or all together; finished steps are skipped. Preview, sort and filter the final table in the app.

highlights.title: Four sources, one table
highlights.body: NCBI RefSeq, GenBank, UniProt and KEGG merged per gene, with every column documented.

highlights.title: Nothing to install first
highlights.body: On first launch the app sets up its own Python. No conda or system Python needed.

highlights.title: Local localisation prediction
highlights.body: DeepLocPro predicts subcellular localisation on your computer.

highlights.title: Resume and batch runs
highlights.body: An interrupted run continues where it stopped. Process many organisms from one CSV.

hardware.Disk: Space for Python and each organism's output
hardware.Network: Needed for first-time setup and to download annotation

name: ChemViewer
tagline: Explore chemical libraries: compound tables, property statistics and library comparisons, all on your computer.
summary: Open a chemical library to browse its compounds, see property distributions and compare it with other libraries. Structure drawing, descriptors and substructure search run locally with RDKit.
It runs well on a laptop. Libraries over 50 MB are read from disk with DuckDB instead of loaded into memory. Large sets are subsampled for analysis, with an option to compute full statistics.

highlights.title: Common file formats
highlights.body: CSV, SDF, SMILES and CXSMILES. Put the files in a folder named after the library.

highlights.title: Fast with large files
highlights.body: Libraries over 50 MB are read from disk, so they open without slowing your computer.

highlights.title: Library-level views
highlights.body: Property statistics, UMAP plots and side-by-side library comparison.

highlights.title: Draw to search
highlights.body: Draw a substructure and filter the library by it.

os.Other: Intel Macs and other systems: build from source with Node.js

name: ChemSketcher
tagline: Draw a molecule and see its properties calculated as you draw.
summary: ChemSketcher is a molecule drawing app built on Ketcher. As you draw, or paste a SMILES string, RDKit calculates properties in a table next to the canvas. Nothing is sent to a web service.
Each molecule on the canvas gets its own row, so you can compare a series as you draw it.

highlights.title: Live properties
highlights.body: SMILES, molecular weight, logP, TPSA, H-bond donors and acceptors, rings, QED and InChIKey.

highlights.title: Several molecules at once
highlights.body: Each molecule on the canvas is detected and listed separately.

highlights.title: Standard file formats
highlights.body: Open and save .mol, .sdf, .ket and .smi files.

highlights.title: Flexible layout
highlights.body: Choose which properties to show, and move, hide or resize the table.

hardware.Disk: About 1 GB for the chemistry engine
